stories.title: Newsletter roundup highlights claims that agents can disprove polysemanticity
stories.summary: Latent Space's AI news roundup flags a claim from researcher Nick Cammarata that AI agents can disprove polysemanticity and meaningfully improve interpretability and alignment.
stories.more: Polysemanticity, the phenomenon where individual neurons in a model represent multiple unrelated concepts, has been a central obstacle for interpretability research. Cammarata's claim, as described in the roundup, suggests that agent-based approaches can disprove aspects of polysemanticity and in turn improve both interpretability and alignment work. The source describes this as a surprising, unanticipated development rather than previously expected research. The excerpt doesn't include the technical basis for the claim or how it was demonstrated.

stories.title: OmniCompass benchmark tests omni-modal video grounding and understanding
stories.summary: Researchers introduce OmniCompass, a benchmark for evaluating multimodal language models on video grounding and understanding across vision-language and omni-modal tracks.
stories.more: The benchmark addresses a gap in existing video evaluation suites, which the authors say cover only part of the relevant evaluation dimensions. OmniCompass defines two tracks: OmniCompass-VL, which assesses vision-language models, and a broader omni-modal track for models that handle additional modalities. The goal is to enable more systematic diagnosis of how well models ground and understand video content. The paper's full benchmark composition and results across specific models aren't detailed in the available excerpt.

stories.title: Waypoint-OPD distills RL policy shifts using early-late agreement signals
stories.summary: A new method, Waypoint-OPD, checks whether early and late shifts in a teacher model's policy during reinforcement learning agree, to improve distillation to student models.
stories.more: Policy-shift distillation normally reuses only the difference between a teacher's pre- and post-RL log probabilities as a training signal for students. The authors argue this endpoint-only view can't tell whether local action preferences changed consistently throughout training, since different shift patterns can produce the same final result. Waypoint-OPD instead checks agreement between early and late teacher policy shifts to gate what gets transferred to the student. The excerpt doesn't specify benchmark results or model sizes tested.

stories.title: Paper formalizes self-evolving agent harnesses that revise their own scaffolding
stories.summary: A new paper formalizes 'harness self-evolution,' where an AI agent revises its own prompts, memory, and workflows over time while keeping the underlying model weights fixed.
stories.more: The framework separates what gets updated, such as interpreted state like prompts, from the mechanisms that propose and admit changes to tools, code, and control logic. Accepted revisions persist across runs, letting the harness accumulate improvements through a feedback-driven process. The authors characterize this as a search problem over possible harness configurations rather than a fixed design. It's part of a growing body of research on improving agents by evolving their scaffolding instead of retraining the underlying model.

stories.title: Speculative Forcing speeds up autoregressive video generation by skipping refinement
stories.summary: Speculative Forcing treats intermediate video frames as drafts and predicts when individual tokens are already close to their final output, skipping unnecessary denoising steps.
stories.more: Few-step autoregressive video generators support streaming generation but typically run every token through the final denoising step regardless of how much refinement it actually needs. The authors found many tokens already closely match their eventual output early on, while others need refinement through to the end. By predicting which tokens can stop early, Speculative Forcing aims to cut redundant computation. The excerpt doesn't give specific speedup numbers or quality comparisons against standard decoding.

stories.title: SCOPE improves text-to-image prompt rewriting by rewarding semantic spans
stories.summary: SCOPE is a reinforcement-learning method for text-to-image prompt rewriting that rewards whole semantic spans, like objects, counts, and attributes, rather than individual words.
stories.more: Existing RL-based prompt rewriters typically apply one image-derived reward signal across individual subword tokens, even though meaning is often carried by coherent phrases like object descriptions or spatial relations. SCOPE, built on Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO), aligns its update weighting with that semantic structure instead. The rewriter jointly generates an enhanced prompt and the credit assignment for its parts. The excerpt doesn't specify which image generator or benchmark was used to validate the approach.

Existing methods typically apply a single signal derived from the image to individual subword tokens, although objects, counts, attributes, and relations form coherent semantic spans. stories.title: Dynamic band splitting lets audio separation models choose their own frequency bounds
stories.summary: A new architecture for audio source separation learns to dynamically split the frequency spectrum per mixture, instead of using the same fixed band boundaries for every input.
stories.more: Band-split architectures keep separation costs manageable by dividing the spectrum into predefined frequency bands encoded as tokens, but conventionally use identical boundaries regardless of the audio content. The authors note that informative spectral structure varies by source, so fixed boundaries can merge important components together or waste resolution where it isn't needed. Their method instead learns where to place band boundaries for each mixture. The excerpt doesn't detail how much this improves separation quality over fixed-band baselines.

items.excerpt: Audio source separation models must preserve fine spectral structure while keeping the cost of the separator tractable. stories.title: 3DCodeVerse gives coding agents a dataset and harness for generating 3D worlds as code
stories.summary: 3DCodeVerse is a research ecosystem, including a 2-million-example dataset, for training coding agents to generate editable, verifiable 3D content as executable code.
stories.more: The project centers on 3DCodeVerse-2M, a large curated dataset of standalone 3D executable code built by collecting open-source data and converting other 3D representations into code form. It also includes a coding harness meant to support spatial reasoning and automated verification of generated 3D content, plus practical guidance for working with 3D code. The goal is to let coding agents create 3D scenes and objects that can be checked for correctness, not just rendered. The excerpt doesn't specify which base models were evaluated on the benchmark.

stories.title: Meta releases Muse Spark Open, an 816B open-weight model tuned for Macs
stories.summary: Meta and Apple jointly released Muse Spark Open, an 816-billion-parameter open-weight multimodal model that runs locally on Mac Studios with Apple's MLX framework.
stories.more: Meta calls it the most capable open-weight model built in the US to date, and it processes text, image, video, and audio with up to a million tokens of context. Working with Apple, Meta optimized the model to run on consumer hardware, specifically two Apple M5 Ultra Mac Studios using the MLX framework, making it one of the first models in its class runnable on a desktop. The Decoder reports it performs roughly on par with top Chinese open-weight models like Qwen, GLM, and Kimi on benchmarks. It's a rare case of Apple and Meta, usually competitors, collaborating directly on model deployment tooling. Pricing, licensing terms for commercial use, and broader availability beyond Mac hardware remain unclear from the announcements.

stories.summary: Anthropic is granting outside evaluator METR employee-level access to review its risk practices and incidents, and has given up the right to block METR's published assessments.

Anthropic's own post frames this as part of a broader push to formalize how independent evaluators oversee frontier AI labs. The arrangement goes further than typical third-party audits by giving METR internal, employee-level visibility rather than limited external review. It follows growing pressure on AI labs to demonstrate credible external oversight rather than self-reported safety claims. Specifics of what METR will have access to, and how often assessments will be published, weren't detailed in the coverage.

stories.more: The experiment explores whether a competitive two-player game can run across two separate phones without a network connection, instead encoding game state as audio chirps exchanged between devices held close together. It's built as static HTML and uses the browser's Microphone API to interpret the chirps. Willison frames it as a playful technical experiment with graphical and gameplay twists added on top of the core chirp-based networking idea. The project is part of his ongoing series of small coding experiments.
